question_text: Marketing research is best defined as
option_a: The systematic gathering, recording and analysis of data about marketing problems
explanation: Marketing research systematically gathers and analyses marketing data.

question_text: Marketing research is important because it
option_a: Helps a business make informed decisions

question_text: One step in marketing research is
option_a: Defining the problem
explanation: Defining the problem is the first step.

question_text: Primary data is
option_a: Data collected first-hand for a specific purpose

question_text: Secondary data is
option_a: Data already collected by others

question_text: One example of primary data is
option_a: Questionnaire responses

question_text: One example of secondary data is
option_a: Newspaper articles

question_text: One advantage of primary data is
option_a: It is specific to the researcher's needs

question_text: One disadvantage of primary data is
option_a: It is expensive and time-consuming to collect
explanation: Primary data is costly to collect.

question_text: One advantage of secondary data is
option_a: It is cheap and quick to obtain
option_b: It is specific to the researcher's needs
explanation: Secondary data is cheap and quick.

question_text: One disadvantage of secondary data is
option_a: It may not suit the researcher's specific needs
explanation: Secondary data may not fit specific needs.

question_text: A survey is
option_a: A method of collecting data by asking questions
explanation: A survey collects data by asking questions.

question_text: One advantage of a survey is
option_a: It can collect data from many people

question_text: One disadvantage of a survey is
option_a: Respondents may give inaccurate answers

question_text: A questionnaire is
option_a: A written set of questions used to collect data
explanation: A questionnaire is a written set of questions.

question_text: One advantage of a questionnaire is
option_a: It can be administered to many people at once

question_text: One disadvantage of a questionnaire is
option_a: It may have a low response rate
explanation: Questionnaires may have low response rates.

question_text: An interview is
option_a: A method of collecting data by asking questions verbally

question_text: One advantage of an interview is
option_a: It allows clarification of questions

question_text: One disadvantage of an interview is
option_a: It is time-consuming

question_text: Observation is
option_a: A method of collecting data by watching behaviour

question_text: One advantage of observation is
option_a: It records actual behaviour

question_text: One disadvantage of observation is
option_a: It cannot explain why behaviour occurs

question_text: An experiment is
option_a: A method of collecting data by testing cause and effect
explanation: An experiment tests cause and effect.

question_text: One advantage of an experiment is
option_a: It can establish cause and effect

question_text: One disadvantage of an experiment is
option_a: It can be expensive and artificial
explanation: Experiments can be costly and artificial.

question_text: A focus group is
option_a: A small group of people brought together to discuss a topic
explanation: A focus group discusses a topic.

question_text: One advantage of a focus group is
option_a: It provides in-depth insights

question_text: One disadvantage of a focus group is
option_a: It may be dominated by one person
explanation: Focus groups may be dominated by one person.

question_text: A sample is
option_a: A subset of a population selected for study
explanation: A sample is a subset of a population.

question_text: Sampling is
option_a: The process of selecting a sample from a population
explanation: Sampling selects a sample from a population.

question_text: One advantage of sampling is
option_a: It saves time and cost

question_text: One disadvantage of sampling is
option_a: It may not be representative of the population

question_text: Random sampling means
option_a: Selecting a sample in which every member of the population has an equal chance

question_text: One advantage of random sampling is
option_a: It reduces bias

question_text: One disadvantage of random sampling is
option_a: It may be difficult to implement
explanation: Random sampling can be hard to implement.

question_text: Stratified sampling means
option_a: Dividing the population into groups and sampling from each group
explanation: Stratified sampling divides the population into groups.

question_text: One advantage of stratified sampling is
option_a: It ensures all groups are represented

question_text: One disadvantage of stratified sampling is
option_a: It requires knowledge of the population structure

question_text: Quota sampling means
option_a: Selecting a sample to match predetermined characteristics

question_text: One advantage of quota sampling is
option_a: It is quick and inexpensive
explanation: Quota sampling is quick and inexpensive.

question_text: One disadvantage of quota sampling is
option_a: It may be biased

question_text: Convenience sampling means
option_a: Selecting a sample from people who are easily accessible
explanation: Convenience sampling uses easily accessible people.

question_text: One advantage of convenience sampling is
option_a: It is quick and cheap
explanation: Convenience sampling is quick and cheap.

question_text: One disadvantage of convenience sampling is
option_a: It may be highly biased

question_text: Data analysis involves
option_a: Organising and interpreting collected data
explanation: Data analysis organises and interprets data.

question_text: One method of data analysis is
option_a: Statistical analysis
explanation: Statistical analysis is a data analysis method.

question_text: A bar chart is
option_a: A graph using rectangular bars to represent data
explanation: A bar chart uses rectangular bars.

question_text: One advantage of a bar chart is
option_a: It makes comparison easy

question_text: A pie chart is
option_a: A circular chart divided into sectors to represent data
explanation: A pie chart is a circular chart divided into sectors.

question_text: One advantage of a pie chart is
option_a: It shows proportions clearly

question_text: A line graph is
option_a: A graph showing trends over time
explanation: A line graph shows trends over time.

question_text: One advantage of a line graph is
option_a: It shows trends clearly

question_text: A marketing research report should include
option_a: Findings and recommendations
explanation: A report includes findings and recommendations.

question_text: One importance of a marketing research report is
option_a: It communicates findings to decision-makers

question_text: One challenge of marketing research is
option_a: High cost

question_text: One ethical issue in marketing research is
option_a: Invasion of privacy
explanation: Invasion of privacy is an ethical issue.

question_text: One way to improve marketing research is
option_a: Using multiple methods

question_text: One difference between marketing research and market research is that
option_a: Marketing research covers all marketing activities while market research focuses on markets
option_d: Marketing research focuses on markets only
explanation: Marketing research is broader than market research.

question_text: One importance of marketing research to product development is
option_a: It identifies features customers want

question_text: One importance of marketing research to pricing is
option_a: It helps determine what customers are willing to pay

question_text: One importance of marketing research to promotion is
option_a: It helps choose the most effective promotional tools

question_text: One importance of marketing research to distribution is
option_a: It helps choose the most effective distribution channels
